info.title: PhoneMail API
info.description: PhoneMail backend MVP contract. Existing /api paths are retained; no /api/v1 prefix is introduced. JSON errors include code, message, requestId and retryable; responses carry X-Request-ID and transient/rate-limit errors may carry Retry-After. Credentialed CORS uses exact CORS_ORIGIN allowlisting. Allowed browser headers include Authorization, X-Auth-Transport, X-CSRF-Token, Idempotency-Key, If-Match, If-None-Match, X-Request-ID, upload headers and Range; exposed headers include Retry-After, X-Request-ID, ETag, Content-Range, Content-Length, Content-Disposition and Accept-Ranges. Phone inputs accept international E.164 or national form with an explicit ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country; no country is inferred. Access tokens expire after 15 minutes; rotating renewal credentials expire after 30 days, with a 90-second encrypted retry window for a lost rotation response. Cookie renewal requires the CSRF cookie value in X-CSRF-Token. Local SMS/IVR and OTP capabilities are distinguished from configured or live-tested providers. E2EE endpoints accept authenticated local PhoneMail user UUIDs and opaque OpenPGP ciphertext; private keys and plaintext stay client-side. Sender/recipient routing IDs and roles, key fingerprints, message and conversation IDs, sync/delivery events, timestamps, and ciphertext size remain visible. Encrypted rows use a generic subject and empty plaintext body. No decrypted server-side search index or malware scanning of encrypted attachments is provided. E2EE content does not route to SMTP providers; ordinary mail retains its existing behavior. Ordinary mail endpoints retain their existing non-E2EE behavior.

post.description: Rotates an opaque bearer refreshToken supplied in the JSON body or the HttpOnly phonemail_refresh cookie. Use exactly one transport; cookie transport requires the CSRF cookie value in X-CSRF-Token. Access credentials expire after 15 minutes and refresh sessions after 30 days. Repeating the immediately previous token within 90 seconds returns the same encrypted cached response; later replay revokes only that session family.

200.description: Key revoked; ciphertext remains stored

post.description: Accepts only local PhoneMail UUID recipients; clients must include the sender public key and each recipient public key in the encryption key set so sender Sent copies are decryptable. Subject, body, attachment names/types/bytes are encrypted inside client PGP/MIME; the server receives ciphertext plus To/CC UUID routing, sender identity, key fingerprints and idempotency metadata only. Conversation/sync IDs, event timing and ciphertext size remain visible. Encrypted messages are stored under a generic subject with an empty plaintext body, are not indexed for plaintext search or malware-scanned as plaintext, and are never queued for SMTP.
